threads: Standings after Wk 8: E720, Ligers and FBT 6-2; Wet Bandits, Wad, BMB and Viva 5-3; DD 4-4; Scally and Bloodfeast 2-6; Nuts and Prestige 1-7.
Streaks: BMB W5, DD W2, Prestige W1 (first win), E720, Wet Bandits, Viva W1; Nuts L7, Bloodfeast L2; FBT's W6 snapped; Ligers, Wad, Scally L1.
Blowout week: five of six games decided by 218+. Closest was BMB over Ligers by 70. Margins: DD +367.75, WB +303, E720 +288.25, Viva +254.25, Prestige +218.75.

Nuts: Wk 8 low 327 (penalty). Started three 0.00s (Zay Flowers, Omar Cooper Jr., Emanuel Wilson). D.J. Moore 78.5 bench. Opt 432.25 still loses. Traded Tony Pollard (159 on their bench in Wk 7) Thursday for Pierre Strong Jr. + $7 of 2027 draft; Pollard 123.5 for E720, Strong 1.00 on Nuts' bench.
E720 over FBT 731.5-443.25, both perfect lineups. Gibbs 137.75, Pollard 123.5 in his first game, Geno 104.5. FBT: Tre Tucker 0.00, Bam Knight 1.50, Higbee 10.50. E720 now first, league-high PF 5,469.

Ligers: benched Kirk Cousins 148.25, started Jayden Daniels (85.75, acquired Wed from Bloodfeast). Also benched Rodriguez 58.25, Wan'Dale 57.75, Malik Washington 55; started Love 11.5, JT 19.5, Metcalf 3. Opt 795.25 wins by 129.5.
BMB: W5. Bhayshul Tuten 143.25, Maye 117.25, Demario Douglas 82. Benched Malik Willis (83.75) again and started Brissett (23.25), which the Wk 8 preview warned about. Won anyway.

Wet Bandits: week high 793. Tee Higgins 191.25, Mahomes 143.25 (after 38.25), Michael Wilson 116.75. Emmett Johnson 128.5 on bench. Caleb Douglas ($391 waiver) 32.25; FAAB now $363. Mumpfield started 0.00.
Scally: Tyler Allgeier 181.5 on the bench; started Carnell Tate (DNP) and Charbonnet 16. Opt 726.75 still loses to 793.

DD: 752.25 over Bloodfeast by 367.75, biggest margin of the week. Benched Bo Nix again (103.5) plus Gainwell 95, Sutton 39.75 = 238.25 bench (241 last week). Opt 903.75. Chase 130.75, Fannin 130.5, Swift 117. Series vs Bloodfeast now 10-10.

Bloodfeast: 384.5, second-lowest. Started Lamar Jackson ($40), 0.00. Benched Kenyon Sadiq (16.50), who belonged in the optimal lineup, a week after starting him for 4.50. Opt 401. Five FA moves in four days.
Viva: Joe Burrow 240.5, week's top player. Jaylen Warren 121.5, Gesicki 82 (the Hurts replacement). Kincaid 89.5 bench. Snapped L2. Series vs Wad now 11-10 Wad.
Wad: benched Cam Ward 138.5, started Deshaun Watson 72. Drake London ($37) 6.00, Jeudy 0.00. Opt 639.75 loses anyway.
Prestige: 1-7, first win, perfect lineup 545.75. Braelon Allen ($1) 128, Kyler 106.

Deadline trades: Bloodfeast sent Diggs + Jayden Daniels to Ligers for Daniel Jones + Adonai Mitchell + $13 2027 auction + 2027 rookie pick; Bloodfeast cut Mitchell a day later. E720 got Pollard from Nuts. Trade deadline has passed.

Wk 8 moves: WB $391 Caleb Douglas; BMB $28 Dylan Sampson (50 on bench; Bloodfeast's $115 buy, cut in Wk 7); Scally $1 Flournoy (55) for McLaurin; FBT added Cooper Kupp (30.25); Bloodfeast added Dulcich, Tank Dell, Travis Hunter (cut 3 days later), Quentin Johnston, Treylon Burks (60.75).

takes.0002: Last week, 130.5 points on the bench and a loss. This week, a perfect lineup and the biggest game of the season turned into a 288-point beating. Entertainment 720 scored 731.5, every point of it, against the team that had won six straight and allowed fewer points than anyone. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 137.75, Geno Smith got the start and scored 104.5, and Tony Pollard, acquired Thursday from Nuts for Pierre Strong Jr., scored 123.5 in his first game. Strong scored 1.00 on Nuts' bench. Jameson Williams (77.5) and Christian Watson (74.75) added the rest. With $0 of FAAB and no waiver budget, 720 found its upgrade at the deadline instead. 6-2, first place, the most points in the league, and the Wet Bandits next.
takes.0005: The streak is over, and it wasn't close. Full Blown Trash set a perfect lineup, 443.25 of 443.25, and lost by 288.25. There's no bench to blame, which is worse. Tre Tucker, who had three straight monster games, scored 0.00. Bam Knight scored 1.50. Tyler Higbee started again and scored 10.50, because some traditions are sacred. Dak Prescott (103.75), James Cook (80.75) and Josh Jacobs (79.25) did what they could. New pickup Cooper Kupp added 30.25. Six straight wins, then the worst possible week against the worst possible opponent. Still 6-2, still in the three-way tie for first, and the Scallywags are next, which should help.
takes.0003: The Ligers traded for a quarterback on Wednesday, then benched the one who scored 148.25. Kirk Cousins sat. Jayden Daniels, fresh from Bloodfeast, started and scored 85.75. That was only the beginning: Chris Rodriguez (58.25), Wan'Dale Robinson (57.75) and Malik Washington (55) also watched from the bench while Jeremiyah Love (11.50), Jonathan Taylor (19.50) and DK Metcalf (3.00) started. The optimal lineup was 795.25. They lost by 70, so the optimal wins by 129.5. Josh Allen scored 142.25 and Brock Bowers 119, and it didn't matter. 6-2, still tied for first, and Bloodfeast, the team that sold them Daniels, is next.
takes.0011: Five straight. BMB beat the Ligers 665.75–595.75 in the closest game of a week full of blowouts. Bhayshul Tuten went for 143.25, Drake Maye threw for 117.25, and Demario Douglas, the $58 waiver pickup the Wet Bandits gave up on, scored 82. Luther Burden added 67. They also benched Malik Willis again (83.75) and started Jacoby Brissett (23.25), which this publication specifically warned against. They won anyway, because the Ligers benched even more. Dylan Sampson, Bloodfeast's former $115 buy, cost $28 and scored 50 on the bench. 0-3 to 5-3. The Diamond Dogs are next.
takes.0004: The Wet Bandits scored 793, the best score of the week, a week after the second-worst. Tee Higgins went for 191.25. Patrick Mahomes went from 38.25 to 143.25. Michael Wilson added 116.75 and Jonah Coleman 92.75. Emmett Johnson scored 128.5 on the bench, and Konata Mumpfield started for 0.00, so the optimal lineup was 921.5, the best possible score in the league. Caleb Douglas, the $391 waiver claim, scored 32.25, which works out to about $12 per point. They have $363 left. 5-3, and next up is 720, the new first-place team.
takes.0007: The Scallywags benched Tyler Allgeier, who scored 181.5. They started Carnell Tate, who didn't play, and Zach Charbonnet, who scored 16. Jahan Dotson scored 71.25 on the bench, a week after starting and scoring 4.50. The good news: the optimal lineup, 726.75, still loses to the Wet Bandits' 793, so the bench only cost them their dignity. Bucky Irving followed last week's breakout with 125, Matthew Golden scored 84.25, and $1 pickup Ryan Flournoy added 55. 2-6, and Trash is next, coming off a 288-point loss and probably in a bad mood.
takes.0010: Prestige won a game. 545.75–327, a perfect lineup, no Penix controversy, no zeros in the starting lineup. Braelon Allen, a $1 running back, scored 128. Kyler Murray, last week's wrong choice, scored 106. Rashee Rice added 64.75 and Chase Brown 52. It helps to play the only team in the league that started three players who scored zero. 1-7, no longer the only winless team in the league. Next is Resistance, and MFL's projections have Prestige favored by 81.7. Nobody tell them.
takes.0006: Nuts scored 327, the lowest in the league, and owes the bitcoin pool. They started Zay Flowers (0.00), Omar Cooper Jr. (0.00) and Emanuel Wilson (0.00). D.J. Moore scored 78.5 on the bench. The optimal lineup, 432.25, still loses by 113.5, so nobody was saving this. And then there's the trade. Last week Nuts benched Tony Pollard's 159 and lost by 10.25. On Thursday they traded him to 720 for Pierre Strong Jr. and $7 of 2027 draft money. Pollard scored 123.5. Strong scored 1.00. Seven straight losses, 1-7, tied with Prestige for the worst record in the league, and the one team they could count on beating just beat them. Wad of Hell is next.
takes.0012: The Diamond Dogs scored 752.25, won by 367.75, the biggest margin of the week, and benched 238.25 points. Again. Bo Nix scored 103.5 on the bench for the second week in a row. Kenneth Gainwell scored 95 there too, and Courtland Sutton 39.75. The optimal lineup was 903.75. Ja'Marr Chase (130.75), Harold Fannin (130.5), D'Andre Swift (117) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (113.5) were too much for Bloodfeast anyway. Two straight wins, back to .500 at 4-4, and the all-time series with Bloodfeast is now 10-10. BMB, the hottest team in the league, is next.
takes.0001: Bloodfeast traded Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs to the Ligers on Wednesday, made five free-agent moves in four days, started Lamar Jackson and got 0.00 from its $40 quarterback. Final: 752.25–384.5, a 367.75-point loss, the worst of the week. Daniel Jones, the quarterback they got back, scored 39.50. Adonai Mitchell, also from that trade, was cut the next day. Travis Hunter was picked up Thursday and cut Sunday for Treylon Burks, who did score 60.75. Puka Nacua (85) tried. And Kenyon Sadiq, started last week for 4.50, sat this week and scored 16.50, enough to make the optimal lineup. The optimal was still only 401. The bitcoin pool got lucky: Nuts was worse. 2-6, and the Ligers, who got Daniels and Diggs, are next.
takes.0009: Joe Burrow scored 240.5. The best individual game of the week by 49 points, more than the Scallywags' whole receiver room. Jaylen Warren added 121.5 and Mike Gesicki, the man Resistance cut Jalen Hurts for, scored 82. Fine. That one worked. T.J. Hockenson (68.5), Derrick Henry (56.75) and Kyren Williams (55.25) chipped in, and Resistance beat Wad of Hell 751.5–497.25 to end a two-game skid. Dalton Kincaid scored 89.5 on the bench, but nobody needed him. 5-3, and the series with Wad is 11-10. Next: Prestige, who are somehow favored.
takes.0008: Wad of Hell benched Cam Ward, who scored 138.5, and started Deshaun Watson, who scored 72. That's the decision that would have been the story, except the optimal lineup (639.75) still loses to Joe Burrow's 240.5-point afternoon. Drake London, a $37 receiver, scored 6.00. Jerry Jeudy scored 0.00. Bijan Robinson ($51) scored 38. Jordan Love (122) and Trey McBride (79) kept it from being embarrassing. It was embarrassing anyway: 751.5–497.25. 5-3, and Nuts are next, who have never been more beatable.

dispatch.head: 720 sets a perfect lineup and ends Trash's streak by 288
dispatch.dek: Entertainment 720 scored 731.5, every available point, and beat Full Blown Trash 731.5–443.25. Tony Pollard, acquired Thursday, scored 123.5 in his first game. Trash also set a perfect lineup; Tre Tucker scored 0.00. E720, the Ligers and Trash are all 6-2, and 720 leads the league in points.

dispatch.kick: Week 8 · Worst Trade of the Deadline
dispatch.head: Nuts trade Tony Pollard, then score 327
dispatch.dek: A week after benching Pollard's 159, Nuts sent him to 720 for Pierre Strong Jr. and $7 of 2027 draft money. Pollard scored 123.5; Strong scored 1.00 on the bench. Nuts started three zeros, posted the week's low score and owe the bitcoin pool. Seven straight losses.

dispatch.head: The Ligers bench Kirk Cousins's 148.25 and lose by 70
dispatch.dek: The Ligers traded for Jayden Daniels on Wednesday and started him (85.75) over Cousins. They also benched three players who scored 55+ while starting Jonathan Taylor (19.50) and DK Metcalf (3.00). The optimal lineup wins by 129.5. BMB has won five straight.

dispatch.head: Tee Higgins scores 191, and the Wet Bandits put up 793
dispatch.dek: A week after scoring 491.5, the Wet Bandits posted the week's best score behind Higgins, Patrick Mahomes (143.25) and Michael Wilson (116.75). The Scallywags benched Tyler Allgeier's 181.5 and still couldn't have caught them.

dispatch.head: Joe Burrow scores 240.5 and Resistance stops the slide
dispatch.dek: Burrow had the week's best game by 49 points, and Resistance beat Wad of Hell 751.5–497.25. Wad benched Cam Ward (138.5) for Deshaun Watson (72), but even its optimal lineup loses.

dispatch.head: Prestige wins its first game
dispatch.dek: A perfect lineup, 545.75, and a 218.75-point win over Nuts. Braelon Allen, a $1 running back, scored 128. Prestige and Nuts are both 1-7.

dispatch.head: Bloodfeast sells to the Ligers, starts a $40 zero and loses by 368
dispatch.dek: Bloodfeast sent Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs to the Ligers for Daniel Jones, Adonai Mitchell, $13 of 2027 auction money and a 2027 rookie pick, then cut Mitchell the next day. Lamar Jackson started and scored 0.00. The Diamond Dogs won 752.25–384.5 with 238.25 on the bench. The Wet Bandits paid $391 for Caleb Douglas (32.25).

Team of the Week.text: 793, the week's top score, a week after scoring 491.5. Tee Higgins 191.25, Mahomes 143.25, Michael Wilson 116.75.

Biggest Bust.text: Traded Tony Pollard for Pierre Strong Jr. Pollard scored 123.5 for 720. Strong scored 1.00. Nuts started three zeros and scored 327.

Luckiest Win.text: Benched Malik Willis again and started Jacoby Brissett (23.25). Won by 70 only because the Ligers benched Kirk Cousins's 148.25.

0004-0002.head: Game of the Week: the new leader hosts the week's high scorer
0004-0002.text: 720 (6-2) just beat Trash by 288 with a perfect lineup and leads the league with 5,469 points. The Wet Bandits (5-3) just scored 793, the best of the week. MFL has 720 by 15.8, the closest spread of the week. The Wet Bandits lead the series 10-6, but 720 has won the last two, 822.25–510.75 last year and 817.75–683.25 in Week 3. Gibbs, Pollard and Geno Smith against Tee Higgins, Patrick Mahomes and Michael Wilson. The Wet Bandits' tiebreaker: start Emmett Johnson this time.

0001-0003.head: Bloodfeast faces its own quarterback
0001-0003.text: Bloodfeast (2-6) sold Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs to the Ligers (6-2) on Wednesday. Now it plays them. MFL has the Ligers by 205.5, the biggest spread of the week. Bloodfeast leads the series 19-15, but the Ligers won the last two, 773–491.25 last year and 608–442.5 in Week 3. The Ligers' biggest threat is their own lineup decisions: Josh Allen, Daniels or Kirk Cousins, who scored 148.25 on the bench last week. Bloodfeast has Daniel Jones.

0012-0011.head: The hottest team in the league against the most frustrating one
0012-0011.text: BMB (5-3) has won five straight. The Diamond Dogs (4-4) have won two straight while benching 479.25 points over those two weeks. MFL has BMB by 44.4. BMB leads the series 14-12, but the Diamond Dogs won Week 3 679–413. Bhayshul Tuten, Drake Maye and Demario Douglas against Ja'Marr Chase, Harold Fannin and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If the Diamond Dogs ever start Bo Nix, this could get ugly.

0005-0007.head: Trash needs a bounce-back, and the Scallywags are right there
0005-0007.text: Trash (6-2) lost by 288 with a perfect lineup. The Scallywags (2-6) benched Tyler Allgeier's 181.5. MFL has Trash by 153.3. The series is 2-2, and Trash won Week 3 786.5–610.25. Dak Prescott, James Cook and Josh Jacobs should be enough, as long as Tre Tucker remembers how to score. For the Scallywags: start Allgeier.

0009-0010.head: Prestige is favored. Really.
0009-0010.text: Prestige (1-7) just won its first game. Resistance (5-3) just got 240.5 from Joe Burrow. MFL has Prestige by 81.7 anyway. Resistance leads the series 17-15 and won Week 3 637.75–507, but Prestige took last year's game 569–461. Braelon Allen and Kyler Murray against Burrow, Jaylen Warren and Mike Gesicki. If Prestige wins two straight, it's no longer a fluke. It's a trend.

0006-0008.head: Nuts try to stop the bleeding
0006-0008.text: Nuts (1-7) have lost seven straight, scored 327 and traded away Tony Pollard. Wad of Hell (5-3) benched Cam Ward's 138.5 last week. MFL has Wad by 123.8. Nuts lead the series 15-12, but Wad has won the last four, including 785.75–577.5 in Week 3. Jordan Love, Trey McBride and Bijan Robinson against Trevor Lawrence, Ashton Jeanty and Jaylen Waddle. Nuts: start D.J. Moore.
